gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a NAS's daily draw at a realistic van duty cycle. At 4 h of drive access and 20 h of hibernation, the QNAP TS-233 uses about 112 Wh, or 8.7 Ah a day from a 12.8 V battery, against 11.3 Ah for the Synology DS223j. ChatGPT only multiplied the active watts by 24 h. None of its results states that the DS223j's Synology Adapter 60W_1 puts out 12 V.
standout_why: I compared against the cited QNAP TS-233 hardware-spec page and the Synology DS223/DS223j and DS124/DS223j compare pages, plus ChatGPT's own table. QNAP publishes 10.81 W typical and 3.43 W disk standby. Synology publishes access and hibernation watts plus a 36 W or 60 W adapter with 100–240 V AC input. None of these pages combines the two modes into a daily Wh or Ah figure. ChatGPT's 259–416 Wh/day assumes 24 h of access, which overstates a mostly idle van NAS by about 2.3×. None states the Synology adapter's DC output voltage, which is why ChatGPT wrote 'Verify adapter'.
decides: The finding confirms the QNAP TS-233 as the pick: at the same duty cycle it uses about 23% fewer Ah per day than the DS223j (8.7 against 11.3), and QNAP itself publishes the 12 VDC input. The DS223j moves from 'verify adapter' to 'also 12 V, per retailer listings of Synology's Adapter 60W_1', so it becomes a real 12 V option. It costs about 2.6 Ah more each day. The finding also gives fuse and DC-DC converter sizes: 4 A for the TS-233 (48 W ÷ 12 V) and 5 A for the DS223j (60 W ÷ 12 V). The DS124 matches the TS-233 on Ah per day, but I could not source its adapter voltage.
